tests.name: Effective description
tests.reasoning: The description uses imperative phrasing ('Use this skill when...'), focuses on user intent (slow storage, alarms firing, production-readiness questions) rather than implementation, lists explicit trigger contexts including cases where the user doesn't name EBS directly ('even if they only say an app or database on EC2 got slower'), explicitly lists metric names and scenarios, and includes an exclusion clause. It is a dense but bounded paragraph, appropriate given the breadth of triggers it needs to cover.
tests.evidence: Use this skill when a user wants to know why Amazon EBS storage is slow, why an EBS alarm fired, or whether their EBS setup is production-ready, even if they only say an app or database on EC2 got slower or ask whether to add IOPS.

tests.name: Verbosity and conciseness
tests.reasoning: The body stays focused on domain-specific procedures (classification table, workflow steps, critical rules) without explaining generic concepts like what EBS or CloudWatch are. It is dense but purposeful.
tests.evidence: Load only the reference files the request needs.

tests.reasoning: No large reference tables, API docs, or error codes are embedded in the body; all detailed material (metrics, thresholds, finding logic) is delegated to references/ files and only linked conditionally.

tests.reasoning: Every file in references/ is linked via markdown link syntax in the body, either in the classification table, Step 2, or the References section at the bottom.

tests.name: Reference links must specify when to load
tests.reasoning: Most reference links specify a triggering condition for when to load them (e.g., specific alarm text, specific user phrasing, or specific judgement needed), rather than generic 'see for details' phrasing.

tests.name: Reference path format
tests.reasoning: All reference paths use the relative 'references/filename.md' format from the skill root with no absolute paths or traversal.

tests.name: Prescription vs description
tests.reasoning: The skill is prescriptive about fragile, consistency-critical operations (read-only enforcement, approval requirements, quota rules) while leaving the diagnostic investigation flexible ('Discover every value from the APIs'), matching specificity to fragility.
tests.evidence: **Read-only.** Changes (ModifyVolume, DeleteSnapshot, quota requests) are proposed with exact parameters, cost and rollback, and run only through operator-approved directed actions

tests.name: Defaults, not menus
tests.reasoning: The classification table routes to one specific reference path per scenario rather than presenting multiple equal tool options; no competing tool menus are presented.

tests.name: Favor procedures over declarations
tests.reasoning: The skill teaches a generalizable classification-and-investigation approach (classify request, load references, discover from APIs, draft report, validate) rather than a one-off instance-specific task.
tests.evidence: Follow the numbered procedure in the loaded path. Discover every value from the APIs. Then draft the report in the format below.

tests.name: Gotchas section
tests.reasoning: Critical Rules section documents concrete non-obvious facts the agent would otherwise get wrong, such as modification limits, baseline checks, and approval requirements.
tests.evidence: **Use current service rules:** up to 4 Elastic Volumes modifications per volume per rolling 24 hours. There is no fixed waiting period between modifications
